Pro: Having a higher clock speed and resolution will result in an OS that is more responsive, and can complete tasks in response time will lead to a more responsive operating system
For instance, having a higher resolution clock allows the CPU to discern the order in which two interrupts were received if they were both sent with little time between them.
If a CPU can run much faster than it’s clock speed, then it can get bottlenecked by multiple interrupts if several of them get queued up within, say, 1ms. Though the CPU might be able to service them all within a fraction of a millisecond, it now has a backlog of interrupts it will have to respond to. This would be quite bad for time critical systems.
Con: Adjusting the OS clock speed requires configuring SysTick, which requires reading up on the documentation. Additionally, some of our code will have to be adjusted, (i.e. scale each value corresponding to time by the clock divisor).
